rv.q: If you live some ways away and have seen this show before, there's not a lot here demanding you see this staging.
This version of Little Shop is entertaining and it is OK to bring the kids.
Marriott’s production understands that behind all of this, Little Shop of Horrors does what all great musical theater should do...

The Marriott Theatre’s Little Shop of Horrors is a darkly funny, sweetly sentimental, visually stunning, musically infectious, unnervingly urgent, stellar production of a strangely wonderful little musical.
This exciting, creatively-directed production is simply sensational.
It’s a tough gig, merging horror, comedy, and social commentary. Little Shop gets all three.
Director Tommy Rapley and the show’s cast and crew have crafted a charming “Little Shop of Horrors” that is somehow hilarious, horrifying and achingly tender.
Altogether a great night out and highly recommended.

It's one of many sly, comic flourishes Rapley introduces throughout this deliciously self-aware production, enthusiastically performed by Marriott's small but mighty cast of singer/actors accompanied by conductor-keyboardist Mason Moss' rock-solid quintet.
This is a bloody good show, and you should definitely make the time to see it.
Marriott’s Lincolnshire has produced an entertaining, farcical, black comedy.
The production was a delightful way to spend an afternoon!

cn.t: Critics praise this production as pitch-perfect and joyfully campy, with standout performances from the three Fates and impressive puppetry. The show delivers earworm songs and sharp satire with polished professionalism.
